title: MyRecon vs Sherlock: Workflow, Cost & Limits
description: Compare Sherlock local CLI research with MyRecon browser access, current scan limits, paid features and public-source verification requirements.
h1: MyRecon vs Sherlock: Workflow, Cost & Limits
intro: Sherlock and MyRecon both help with public username research, but their access models differ. Sherlock is an open-source command-line project you run in your own environment. MyRecon offers a browser workflow with guest previews, account limits and optional paid features. Neither tool establishes who owns a matching profile.

sections.heading: Sherlock: local installation and command-line output
sections.body: Sherlock's official repository documents installation with pipx install sherlock-project and a search with sherlock followed by a username. Check that repository before installation for current supported environments and options. Local execution is useful when you need repeatable commands, script integration or output files under your own control. You are responsible for dependency updates, request behavior and reviewing results. The project is free open-source software; that does not guarantee reliable responses from every third-party platform.

sections.heading: MyRecon: browser access and explicit plan limits
sections.body: The MyRecon standard release catalogue has 500+ platforms. Guests see a limited preview; signed-in free accounts get five standard scans per day. The optional one-time pack (₹99 via Indian checkout, or US$3.99 via enabled international checkout) adds unlimited standard scans, Deep Search access and ten Extended scans over a separate 3,000+ catalogue. Credits do not expire and the pack has no automatic renewal. The Android listing is in closed testing for eligible testers. Browser and Android availability should therefore not be presented as identical. The pricing page describes the current offer.

sections.heading: Compare the same question and inspect the sources
sections.body: Use the same handle you control and record the date, each tool's version or release, chosen scope, result status and original profile URL. Keep unsupported, blocked and unknown checks separate from negatives. A catalogue count describes scope, not successful checks or confirmed accounts. This page does not publish a same-scope Sherlock benchmark and makes no speed, coverage superiority or accuracy claim. The homepage's recorded username case has a different scope and cannot settle this comparison.

sections.heading: Worked decision: a one-off self-audit or scripted review
sections.body: For a one-off self-audit on a browser-only device, MyRecon can surface candidates without a local installation. Open each result and confirm your own accounts through saved records. For a repeatable local command pipeline, Sherlock may fit better if you can maintain its environment. If the key requirement is private-profile access or identity verification, neither username workflow satisfies it. Keep that missing requirement visible rather than choosing by the largest advertised site count.

sections.heading: Data handling and operational limits
sections.body: A local Sherlock search still sends requests to third-party sites. A browser-based MyRecon search uses its hosted services and the data handling described in the privacy policy. Do not describe either workflow as anonymous merely because it has no local signup step. Platform rate limits, login walls and changing templates affect both. Use bounded authorized searches, and keep your exports and screenshots under the same access and retention controls as other research notes.

faq.question: Is MyRecon entirely free and ad-supported?
faq.answer: No. It has free guest previews and a signed-in daily standard allowance, plus optional paid features. See current pricing for the ₹99 scan pack.

faq.question: Does this comparison prove one tool finds more accounts?
faq.answer: No. No same-scope Sherlock benchmark is published here. Counts, methods and source availability differ.

faq.question: When is Sherlock a better fit?
faq.answer: Consider it when you need a local command-line workflow or script integration and can manage installation, dependencies and source review.

migration_note: Keep a local Sherlock workflow if its script integration matters. Evaluate MyRecon on an authorized handle with source review before changing your process.
method: Worked examples are illustrative unless explicitly labeled as observed. Product limits were checked against the release source; linked provider instructions describe external workflows, not a claim that every account flow was tested.
